bio05: Nutrients have functions beyond supplying fuel. Mechanical fragmentation changes particle size, while enzymatic hydrolysis changes molecules. A negative starch test does not prove that all products are glucose. Absorption must cross the epithelium.

Food travels along the digestive lumen, not through liver or pancreas tissue. Liver produces bile and gallbladder stores it. Bile salts assist emulsification rather than acting as lipase. Enzyme source, site of activation and site of action must be separately labeled.

Villi and microvilli require separate magnification scales. Typical monosaccharides and amino acids enter portal blood pathways. Long-chain lipid products are processed into chylomicrons that initially enter lymph. Luminal micelles are not the same particles as chylomicrons.

Glycolysis turns one six-carbon glucose into two three-carbon products and has the stated net direct yield2ATP after investment. Lactate formation recycles NAD plus and must not earn the same ATP twice. Mitochondrial inner-membrane pathways and cytosolic glycolysis are distinct.

Separate amino nitrogen from carbon skeletons during amino-acid breakdown. Liver-associated urea synthesis precedes blood transport and kidney excretion. Urea containing two nitrogen atoms is not proof of a single-step reaction of two free-ammonia molecules.

Split glycerol from fatty-acid metabolism. A saturated16-carbon even-chain fatty acid yields8acetyl units over7beta-oxidation rounds in the stated model. Even-chain fatty-acid acetyl-CoA does not ordinarily yield net glucose in humans; glycerol can contribute differently.

Connect metabolic nodes without drawing every arrow as reversible. Account separately for carbon, nitrogen and energy. Glucose complete oxidation has RQ1; palmitic-acid complete oxidation consumes23oxygen and produces16carbon dioxide, giving16/23. State the model limits.
bio06: Compare cubes of side1and2cm. Area rises4fold but volume8fold, so surface-to-volume ratio falls from6to3percm. Under the same simple diffusion model characteristic time scales with distance squared, while bulk transport still requires terminal exchange.

Show systemic return to right atrium, right ventricle, pulmonary artery, lungs, pulmonary vein, left atrium, left ventricle and aorta. Arteries are away from the heart irrespective of oxygenation. Valves respond to pressure gradients.

Signal starts at the sinoatrial node, passes through atrial pathways and the AV node delay, then the conduction bundles and Purkinje system. Electrical activity is not the blood-flow route or a direct pressure trace. Neural modulation is not mandatory brain triggering of every beat.

Distinguish wall-associated atherosclerotic plaque, locally formed thrombus and a traveling embolus. Coronary vessels supply myocardium. A risk change2percent to1percent is1percentage point absolute and50percent relative, not50percentage points.

Separate xylem from living phloem sieve elements and companion cells. Source and sink roles depend on stage. Different phloem pathways can transport in opposite directions without showing a single bulk stream flowing both directions at once.

Xylem transpiration tension differs from phloem source-sink pressure flow. Water moves from higher total water potential to lower, so-0.2MPa to-0.8MPa. Potometer uptake Ad/t is a proxy and must account for storage and other losses.
chem19: Define reaction system, solution and calorimeter separately. An exothermic reaction has negative reaction heat while warming solution absorbs positive heat. Include calorimeter heat capacity and any outward loss explicitly.

For N2+3H2 forming2NH3, the given reaction enthalpy-92kJ belongs to the whole written equation. One mole ammonia corresponds to-46kJ; reversing and doubling gives+184kJ. Conditions and phases must remain consistent.

Standard formation enthalpy refers to1mol of specified product from reference-state elements. A zero reference value is not zero total energy. Compute products minus reactants with stoichiometric coefficients and matching states.

Combustion enthalpy is negative for exothermic combustion, while heating value is often a positive magnitude. Condensing product water adds released heat. Useful energy equals efficiency times released magnitude; incomplete combustion changes the final state.

Neutralization heat is based on moles of water formed. Strong-acid strong-base net reaction is H plus plus OH minus forming water under specified dilute conditions. Count limiting equivalents and total solution mass; weak-electrolyte and dilution effects are separate.

Hess combinations must reverse signs and scale enthalpies with equations. In the stated carbon cycle,-394 equals-111 plus-283kJ. Matching formulas with different phases cannot cancel. Average-bond estimation is broken bonds minus formed bonds, not a precise reaction mechanism.

For50MJ input and60percent efficiency, useful energy is30MJ and other output20MJ. Do not double-count recovered heat. Compare emissions per useful energy and state the system boundary; local zero carbon dioxide is not lifecycle zero emissions.
phys15: Label equilibrium P,V,T and gas amount independently. Absolute pressure equals ambient plus signed gauge pressure. Convert liters to cubic meters and Celsius to kelvin before ratios. Sealed is not necessarily rigid; a rigid open vessel can change amount.

Match mole amount n with R and particle count N with Boltzmann constant k. PV=nRT=NkT, N=nNA. SI pressure-volume is joules. The equation of state does not determine process heat or work and is only an approximation for real gases.

Two nonreacting rigid chambers at the same temperature and with no external leak conserve total gas amount.2L at200kPa and3L at100kPa yield140kPa in5L. Density trends depend on which constraints are fixed.

At fixed amount and temperature the absolute-pressure versus-volume plot is hyperbolic; pressure versus reciprocal volume is linear. Include apparatus dead volume. Gauge pressures cannot be directly multiplied by volume as a conserved product.

At fixed amount and volume absolute pressure is proportional to kelvin temperature. A Celsius plot is shifted. Real-gas low-temperature condensation can invalidate the extrapolation. Heating changes particle motion rather than scaling particle radii.

A loaded frictionless equilibrium piston can maintain fixed pressure only under its stated force conditions. Starting2L at300K, expansion to a3L stop reaches450K; subsequent fixed-volume heating to600K gives final pressure4/3of the original.
phys19: Prism internal angles satisfy r1+r2=A and deviation delta=i+e-A. Minimum deviation is a special symmetric transmitted path. Stationary-interface ordinary refraction preserves frequency, while speed and wavelength change. Normal visible dispersion bends violet more than red in the stated glass.

Separate continuum, emission-line and absorption-line arrangements. Absorption needs the appropriate background and gas path. Photon energy is hf=hc/lambda, not proportional to wavelength. Unspecified lines are teaching schematics, not invented measured element spectra.

Use the stated real-positive lens convention. Converging f10cm with u30cm gives v15cm,m-0.5; with u6cm gives v-15cm,m2.5. Diverging f-12cm with u24cm gives v-8cm,m1/3. Real rays and virtual extensions differ.

For lens displacement use fixed object-screen separation D and lens-position difference d, f=(D squared-d squared)/(4D). D100cm,d60cm gives f16cm and conjugate distances80and20cm. Two real-image positions require D>4f; use a safe ordinary light source.
phys10: Six same-side peaks define five cycles. A full one-dimensional cycle has path4A but zero displacement, and peak-to-peak is2A. Equal position with opposite velocity is not the same phase.

Net acceleration is minus omega squared times displacement from equilibrium. Restoring acceleration opposes displacement, not necessarily velocity. For a vertical spring the equilibrium origin includes static gravity extension; a pendulum is harmonic only under the stated small-angle approximation.
For x=Acos(omega*t+phi), velocity is-A*omega*sin and acceleration is-omega squared*x. Initial x0.03m and v-0.20m/s with omega5 require amplitude0.05m and first-quadrant phi with cosine0.6,sine0.8.

Time graphs x,v,a use a common time axis and different vertical units. At a positive displacement peak velocity is zero and acceleration is negative maximum. A spatial wave snapshot is not a temporal oscillator graph.

Effective potential0.5kx squared and kinetic energy sum to0.5kA squared in the undamped model. Energy gives speed, not velocity sign. Halving corresponding turning-point amplitude leaves one-quarter mechanical energy.

For m1,k100,F0=2 and viscous b2, amplitude at driving omega10 is0.10m, but the precise nonzero displacement peak is at square-root98rad/s. Increasing b to4 gives0.05m at omega10. Fixed steady amplitude still requires nonzero average input and dissipation.
chem24: In a galvanic Zn/Cu model, Zn is the negative oxidation anode and Cu is the positive reduction cathode. Electrons travel externally from Zn to Cu; ions, not electrons, carry current through the salt bridge. Anions move to the anode compartment and cations to the cathode compartment in this model.

Use standard reduction potentials, Ecell=Ecathode-Eanode. Multiplying a balanced half-equation does not multiply its potential. State the specified standard conditions; standard potential is not automatically an operating voltage.

Distinguish capacity in Ah from energy in Wh. A 3.7V,2Ah constant-voltage illustration stores7.4Wh or26640J. In a lead-acid model both plates can form PbSO4 during discharge through different redox half-reactions.

For molten and aqueous electrolytes, show the phase, possible competing species and electrode material. Anode always means oxidation and cathode reduction; their electrical signs differ between electrolytic and galvanic cells. Do not imply that aqueous NaCl deposits sodium metal.

In electroplating the workpiece is the cathode. Soluble-anode replenishment depends on the stated process. Electrorefining impurity fates depend on their chemistry; aluminium extraction uses molten electrolyte rather than aqueous reduction.

Faraday accounting uses Q=It, electron amount Q/F, balanced electron ratio and current efficiency. With F96500C/mol,1930C supplies0.020mol electrons and deposits0.635g Cu at100percent efficiency for Cu2+ reduction. Gas volumes require explicit temperature and pressure.

Show spatially separated iron oxidation and oxygen reduction in aerated neutral water, with electron conduction in metal and ionic transport in water. Rust is not universally pure anhydrous Fe2O3. Salt can accelerate corrosion but is not an absolute requirement.

Distinguish barrier coatings, passivation and sacrificial protection. Zinc can act sacrificially to iron under specified conditions; a scratched copper coating can make exposed iron a local anode. Do not reverse the protected metal and sacrificial anode.
phys09: For fixed-axis rigid rotation, all points share angular velocity but tangential speed is radius times angular velocity. Tangential acceleration r alpha and inward radial acceleration r omega squared are perpendicular components.120rpm equals4pi rad/s.

Draw each mass with its perpendicular distance to the stated axis. Moment of inertia depends on that axis. The parallel-axis relation starts at a parallel centre-of-mass axis; disk and ring formulas must identify their distinct mass distributions.

Pure rolling on a fixed surface combines centre-of-mass translation and rotation about the centre of mass. vCM=omega R requires no slip. Do not count translation twice when changing the reference axis.

Torque uses the perpendicular lever arm from the reference axis to the force line. A freely rolling uniform disk down a30degree slope with g10 has acceleration10/3m/s2; for mass2kg the uphill static friction is10/3N, only if the friction limit permits.

Angular momentum about a point is r cross p, with the right-hand direction. Fixed-axis L=I omega is the stated axis component, not a universal assertion that all three-dimensional L vectors parallel omega. Radial motion can have zero angular momentum while retaining kinetic energy.

Angular momentum is conserved only about a reference with the appropriate negligible net external torque. Pulling mass inward can increase rotational energy through internal work. Inelastic coupling of coaxial disks conserves total angular momentum but generally loses mechanical kinetic energy.
phys20: Connect each optical model with evidence and its domain. Geometric straight-line propagation can be a short-wavelength limit of waves, so a sharp shadow alone does not uniquely prove classical corpuscles. Dark interference regions represent redistribution, not destruction of total energy.

Distinguish slit separation d, slit width a and screen distance L. Include initial phase in total phase difference. Unequal input intensities I0 and4I0 give maximum9I0 and minimumI0, not complete extinction. Paraxial fringe spacing is lambda L/d.

Single-slit dark fringes satisfy a sin theta=m lambda for nonzero integers; the centre is bright. Central near-axis width is2lambda L/a. Grating principal maxima instead satisfy d sin theta=m lambda, with geometric bound abs(m lambda)<=d. A500line/mm grating has d2micrometres.

Polarization axes follow the transverse electric field, not the propagation ray. For originally unpolarized I0 through ideal0,45,90degree polarizers, successive intensities are I0/2,I0/4,I0/8. Brewster reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular under the stated interface assumptions.

Use a right-handed mutually perpendicular electric field, magnetic field and propagation triad, with E cross B forward. Vacuum frequency increases as wavelength decreases while all spectral bands share c. Photon energy hf differs from total beam power; spectral boundaries can overlap.

A reflector at distance D gives total return path2D. Subtract calibrated electronics delay before dividing. In the specified equal-tooth-gap wheel model, first adjacent-tooth extinction takes1/(2Nf), giving c=4DNf. Label numerical examples as illustrative, not historical measurements.
chem28: For acyclic hydrocarbons with exactly one C=C, use CnH2n for n at least2. Each neutral carbon has total bond order4. Show one sigma and one pi bond, locally planar sp2 geometry near120degrees, and distinguish a molecular formula from unique connectivity.

Enumerate only the stated domain: acyclic C4H8 has3 constitutional alkenes, or4 species when cis and trans but-2-ene are separate. Each double-bond carbon must have two different substituents for the relevant geometric isomerism. Reversing a chain drawing does not add an isomer.

Choose an appropriate longest parent containing C=C and number the double bond low before side-group locants in the simple monoalkene examples. CH2=CHCH(CH3)CH2CH3 is3-methylpent-1-ene, with5 parent carbons but6 total carbons. Verify every valence.

Separate low water solubility from density. In the given illustrative liquid,0.75g/mL times50mL gives37.5g; if immiscible with water near1g/mL it forms an upper layer. Ideal gas density PM/RT applies only with stated phase, temperature and pressure; qualitative trends are not invented measured data.

Complete combustion of CnH2n consumes3n/2 O2 and produces nCO2 and nH2O. For10mL propene with60mL O2 at equivalent ideal-gas conditions,45mL O2 is consumed, leaving15mL O2 plus30mL CO2 after water removal. Do not count condensed water as dry gas.

Ordinary alkene addition retains the C-C sigma skeleton while replacing the pi bond with new bonds. Non-aqueous simple bromine addition gives vicinal dibromides; aqueous competing pathways and other bromine-consuming substances limit diagnostic specificity. Mark ionic versus radical HBr conditions before assigning regional preference.

Distinguish mild hydroxylation, strong oxidative cleavage and ozonolysis workup. Track each original double-bond carbon. Under the specified strong-oxidation model, but-2-ene yields two ethanoic-acid fragments;2-methylbut-2-ene gives acetone plus ethanoic acid. Account for terminal-carbon CO2 and all carbon atoms.

In polypropene the repeating unit is [-CH2-CH(CH3)-]n, with single backbone bonds and the methyl side group preserved. Extend chain bonds through both bracket edges. An average chain mass42000 with unit42 implies approximate average degree1000, not identical length for every chain. Simple addition polymerization does not release one water per unit.

Distinguish physical fractional distillation from chemical cracking or elimination. Ethanol dehydration gives ethene plus water in the stated catalysed model;9.2g ethanol theoretically yields5.6g ethene and80percent isolated mass yield gives4.48g. Gas volumes need explicit T and P; cracking equations are illustrative channels rather than unique product spectra.
chem32: Classify by the hydroxyl attachment: benzyl alcohol C6H5CH2OH is an alcohol, whereas C6H5OH is phenol. Count hydroxyl groups separately from the carbon neighbours of the OH-bearing carbon.2-methylpropan-2-ol has three carbon neighbours at that carbon and no attached hydrogen.

Distinguish intermolecular hydrogen bonds from covalent O-H bonds using dashed versus solid lines. Neutral alcohol oxygen has two ordinary covalent bonds. Long hydrocarbon segments can limit water solubility. Closed-system masses add, but pure-liquid volumes need not add to the final mixture volume.

Show separate alcohol pathways and their conditions: primary alcohol to aldehyde or acid, secondary alcohol to ketone, and no automatic same-skeleton carbonyl from tertiary alcohol.2ROH with2Na gives2RONa plusH2 in the specified dry model; water is an interfering source of hydrogen.

Preserve carbon skeleton and OH position when mapping preparation routes. Ordinary acid hydration of propene mainly gives propan-2-ol; acetone reduction also gives propan-2-ol. The net fermentation equation glucose to2ethanol plus2CO2 is not a one-step mechanism. Separate conversion, selectivity and product recovery.

Draw methanol, ethanol, ethylene glycol and glycerol with respective molar masses32,46,62,92g/mol and OH counts1,1,2,3. For9.2g samples, glycerol contains0.30mol OH versus ethanol0.20mol OH. Product uses are conditional and never imply drinkability or universal safety.

Phenol has an OH directly on aromatic carbon. Separate neutral phenol dissolution, melting and chemical conversion to phenoxide. Acidification can produce dissolved neutral phenol without a visible precipitate when below solubility. Do not depict illustrative solubility values as measured constants.

Phenol plus OH- forms phenoxide plus water. Carbonate and hydrogen carbonate are different bases and require the correct acid-base pair. In the specified excess bromine-water model, substitute ring H at2,4,6 to give tribromophenol plus3HBr from3Br2; retain the aromatic skeleton and account for all six bromine atoms.

Cumene is C6H5CH(CH3)2, not n-propylbenzene. Show a correctly connected hydroperoxide intermediate and condition-labelled cleavage to phenol plus acetone. The net balance C9H12+O2 toC6H6O+C3H6O gives120+32=94+58g, and is not a single-step or operational safety diagram.
chem15: Distinguish neutral diatomic halogens X2 from halide ions X-. In Cl2+2Br- to2Cl-+Br2, chlorine gains2electrons and two bromide ions lose2electrons. Molecular phase trends involve intermolecular forces rather than simply breaking internal halogen bonds.

Balance MnO2+4HCl toMnCl2+Cl2+2H2O for the stated concentrated-acid model. Only two of four chloride atoms are oxidized; the other two remain in MnCl2. Separate impurity removal, drying, target collection and final waste-gas absorption. Do not depict uncontrolled toxic-gas release.

For the specified concentrated-brine membrane cell, oxidize chloride at the positive anode and reduce water at the negative cathode. Electrons stay in the external circuit; ions cross the membrane. Chlorine and hydrogen outlets stay separate. Aqueous Na+ migration is not sodium-metal deposition.

HCl gas is molecular, while aqueous hydrochloric acid contains hydronium and chloride. Acid mist consists of liquid droplets, whereas HCl with NH3 forms solid NH4Cl smoke. Acid strength and concentration are different properties. Chloride detection alone does not identify hydrochloric acid.

Keep the NaHSO4-forming and Na2SO4-forming preparation equations with their corresponding conditions rather than combining their coefficients. Separate generated HCl from absorbed HCl and final solution concentration. Absorption pressure drops can cause backflow, so flow arrows and protective concepts must be physically consistent.

AgCl,AgBr andAgI have different precipitation and ammonia-complexation behaviour; AgF is not the same insoluble-salt case. Complexation lowers free Ag+ while total dissolved silver can rise. Do not acidify a chloride test with HCl and attribute all precipitation to the original sample.

For HClO,HClO2,HClO3,HClO4, chlorine oxidation numbers are+1,+3,+5,+7. Cold dilute alkali gives chloride and hypochlorite in a1:1Cl-atom split; the stated hot concentrated model gives chloride and chlorate in a5:1split. Acid strength, oxidation tendency and kinetic rate are distinct.
phys17: Distinguish particle oscillation from phase propagation in transverse and longitudinal mechanical waves. A longitudinal displacement-versus-position sine plot is not a literal transverse path. For a periodic wave v=f lambda and T=1/f; the phase advances one wavelength per period.

In the stated340m/s medium,40kHz ultrasound has wavelength8.5mm. Echo time includes the return path2D. Sound intensity level is logarithmic: two independent incoherent60dB sources give about63.01dB, not120dB. Specify reference intensity, medium and conditions.

Plot displacement versus position at fixed time separately from displacement versus time at fixed position. For right-travelling y=F(x-vt), a positive spatial slope means negative particle velocity. Peak-to-trough displacement is2A. Two snapshots can differ by an unknown integer number of wavelengths.

For y=0.020sin(4pi x-20pi t) with SI coordinates, wavelength0.50m, frequency10Hz and phase speed5m/s to+x. At x=t=0 the transverse particle velocity is-0.4pi m/s, not the phase speed. Initial zero displacement alone does not select a unique velocity sign.

Label angles from the interface normal and distinguish the plotted wave variable. Fixed-end string displacement reflects with inversion; free-end displacement does not. At a stationary interface frequency stays fixed, and sin(theta1)/v1=sin(theta2)/v2. Energy coefficients are not arbitrary displacement-amplitude ratios.

For equal opposite waves y=2A sin(kx)cos(omega t), adjacent nodes are lambda/2 apart and node-to-antinode spacing is lambda/4. Both-fixed strings allow all positive integer modes; ideal one-open-one-closed pipes allow odd modes. A closed pipe end is a displacement node and pressure antinode.

Distinguish a moving observer, which changes wavefront encounter rate, from a moving source, which changes wavelength in the medium. With sound speed340m/s and source500Hz, observer approach20m/s gives529.41Hz, while source approach20m/s toward a fixed observer gives531.25Hz. Define signed velocities relative to the medium and state the subsonic assumptions.
phys18: Measure reflection angles from the normal. A plane mirror at x=0 images an object at x=-2m to x=2m; the object-image distance is4m. Real reflected rays are solid and directed, while mirror-backward virtual extensions are dashed and do not carry real rays behind the mirror.

Use one explicit paraxial mirror convention: real object distance positive; concave f positive,convex f negative; real image in front v positive and virtual behind v negative. Concave f10cm,u30cm gives v15cm,m=-0.5; u5cm gives v=-10cm,m2. Convex f=-10cm,u20cm gives v=-20/3cm,m1/3. Mirrors reflect rather than transmitting lens rays.

At a stationary transparent interface, n1 sin i=n2 sin r with angles from the normal and frequency unchanged. Air to n1.5 glass at30degrees gives r19.47degrees; vacuum600nm becomes400nm in that medium. An out-of-range refracted sine signals no ordinary propagating solution, not a value to clamp.

Near-normal apparent depth12cm through n1.5 material viewed from air is8cm; backward extensions locate a virtual image without moving the object. For a parallel slab of normal thickness5cm,i60degrees,r30degrees and equal outside media, lateral shift is5/sqrt3 cm. Distinguish normal thickness from internal slant path and state near-axis limitations.

Total internal reflection needs high-to-low index and internal incidence strictly above critical. Glass1.5 to air at45degrees qualifies with critical41.81degrees; the same glass to water4/3 at45degrees does not, because critical62.73degrees. Fibre input acceptance angle is not the side-wall critical angle. No ordinary far-field refracted ray is drawn beyond the TIR boundary.

For a refractive-index graph with vertical sin i and horizontal sin r, slope is nsample/noutside; reversing axes reverses the ratio. Angles are from the normal. Radial passage through an ideal semicircular block is normal at the curved surface. Repeatability does not remove systematic normal-line error, and illustrative supplied values must not be labelled measured data.
